name: SASL
note: Turner's pure ISWIM-derived language; redesigned for lazy evaluation in 1976
typeSystem: Untyped. In 'St Andrews Static Language', 'static' referred to the absence of commands and mutable defined data structures, not to static typing.
runtime: The 1976 lazy SASL implementation used a lazy SECD machine. After moving to Kent in 1977, Turner reimplemented SASL by compiling it to SK combinators evaluated through graph reduction; that approach was published in 1979 and influenced Miranda and, through it, Haskell.

runtimes.name: Lazy SECD machine / graph-reduction interpreter
runtimes.role: The 1976 system used a lazy SECD machine; the later Kent implementation lazily reduced a shared graph of compiled SK combinators.

compilers.name: SASL compiler (David Turner)
compilers.role: In the post-1977 Kent implementation, compiled SASL source to SK combinators for the graph-reduction interpreter.

codeExample.caption: Conditional expression using SASL's -> ; syntax
codeExample.source:
def fact n = n = 0 -> 1 ; n * fact (n - 1)

fact 10
